doc.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Armstrong at his peak in the mid-1950s
summary: He thought Armstrong at his peak when recorded; Wynton Marsalis rates those records highest.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And when he was doing those, is it so that he had reached his – he felt at least he had reached his peak, and his trumpet, he wasn’t able to do then what he did before?
I never felt that way. He never said anything about it. Because after all, when I recorded him in the middle ’50s, I thought that he was at the absolute peak of his powers.
Oh yeah. For instance, Wynton Marsalis tells people that the recordings I made were the greatest that Louis made in his life after the 1930s, early ’30s.
That Tiger Rag that you mentioned . . .
The flamboyant one on OKeh Records.
Yeah. What he does on that is . . .
